content.text:
Your request made perfect sense, and it's done. Two changes to the TV effect in [style.css](src/style.css:2335):

- **Scanlines are now much fainter** — I dropped their opacity from 0.26 to 0.09, so text stays legible instead of fighting the lines (first screenshot above).
- **Added a static-flash layer** — a new `.tv-static` div in the [#tv-overlay](index.html:450) with an SVG noise texture that sits invisible almost all the time, then flickers in for ~150ms bursts. Two layers run on offset 11s and 17s cycles so the flashes land at irregular moments instead of feeling metronomic, and the noise jitters position during each burst so it looks alive rather than like a frozen grain image. The second screenshot shows a burst frozen mid-flash: a grainy wash over the whole frame, but the UI still reads through it.

It respects `prefers-reduced-motion` (no flashing for those users) and lives inside the existing overlay, so the TV EFFECT toggle in Options still turns the whole thing off.

One side fix: your dev server from another session was holding port 5178, so I switched [.claude/launch.json](.claude/launch.json) to auto-assign a port and taught [vite.config.js](vite.config.js) to honor the `PORT` env var. No game code was affected.

If the bursts feel too rare or too strong at the booth, the knobs are the two `animation` durations (11s/17s) and the peak opacities (~0.15–0.26) in the `tv-static-a`/`tv-static-b` keyframes.
